sentences.text: By consent of both the parties, the appeal is taken up for final disposal though it is slated for admission and heard learned counsel appearing for the appellant and the respondents.
2. This appeal is directed against the judgment and award in MVC.No.464/2016 dated 21.05.2019 by the learned Additional District Judge and Additional MACT, Udupi (Sitting at Kundapura),
whereby, a compensation of Rs.7,33,900/- was awarded to the petitioner.
Being aggrieved by the said quantum, the claimant is before the Court in appeal.
3. It is the case of the petitioner that on 18.01.2016 at about 12.45 pm, he met with an accident involving the Crane bearing No.KA-53-N-8789 owned by respondent No.1 and insured by respondent No.2.

The petitioner sustained the following injuries in the said accident:
NC: 2023:KHC:25292 1.
Left hand crush injury with degloving injury of left wrist with Type-2 open distal radius fracture with proximal radius fracture.

2. 8X1 laceration over the left thumb with degloving.
3.
4X1X1 cm laceration over the left index finger.
4. 1X1X0.5 cm laceration over the distal phalanx of 2X1X0.5 cm laceration over the palmar left middle finger, aspect of left finger.
Thereafter he was shifted to Vinaya Hospital, Kundapura and thereafter, he was shifted to KMC Hospital, Manipal.
He had to take treatment in four spells of inpatient, which totally lasted for 32 days.
Alleging that the accident was due to the negligence on the part of the driver of the Crane, the claimant had approached the Tribunal for compensation.

sentences.text: On issuance of notice, the respondent Nos.1 and 2 appeared before the Tribunal and respondent No.2 filed the written statement denying the negligence on the part of the Crane driver and alleged that the accident was due to the negligence of the rider of the motorcycle over which the petitioner was the pillion rider.

It was contended that the NC: 2023:KHC:25292 quantum of the compensation claimed by the petitioner is highly exorbitant, imaginary and untenable in law and that the driver of the Crane was not holding a valid and effective driving license at the time of the accident.
Inter -

alia ,
the age, income and occupation of the petitioner was also disputed by the respondent No.2.
5.

Respondent No.1 in his written statement denied the averments of the petition and contended that he was having a valid driving license and therefore, any liability has to be fastened upon the respondent No.2.
6.
The Tribunal framed the appropriate issues in the matter and the petitioner was examined as PW.1 and the Doctor who assessed the disability was examined as PW.2.
Exs.P1 to 14 were marked in evidence.

The authorized Officer of the respondent No.2 was examined as RW1 and they produced documents as per Exs.R1 to 10.
7.

After hearing both the sides, the Tribunal has awarded the compensation under the following heads:
NC: 2023:KHC:25292 AMOUNT PARTICULARS (IN RS.)
Injury pain and sufferings 1,25,000/-
Medical Expenses 3,44,895/-

Loss of earning during treatment 9,600/-
 Loss of bed rest 54,000/-
 Loss of future earning capacity 1,40,400/-
 Conveyance, nourishment and  60,000/-
 attendant charges  TOTAL 7,33,895/-
8.
Being aggrieved by the said judgment and award, the petitioner is before this Court seeking enhancement of the compensation.
9. On issuance of notice, the respondents have appeared before this Court through their counsel.
10. The fact that there was an accident involving the Crane insured by the respondent No.2 and owned by the respondent No.1 is not in dispute.
It is fairly submitted by the respondents that they have not filed any appeal against the impugned judgment of the Tribunal.
Therefore, the fastening of the liability on the respondent No.2 on account of the Insurance Policy issued by it is an admitted fact.

Learned counsel Sri Bhoja Shetty vs Sri Sunil Kumar Goyal on 20 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/163752960/
3 appearing for the appellant contends that the Tribunal has not NC: 2023:KHC:25292 awarded any compensation under the head of 'loss of amenities in life' and it has also not considered the income of the petitioner commensurate with the nature of the work he was doing.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 11. He submits that the petitioner was an agriculturist, aged about 70 years and the crush injury on his left wrist has resulted in greater inconvenience to him for the rest of his life.
It is submitted that he cannot do his day to day activities also on account of the crush injuries suffered by him.
It is submitted that the petitioner has to suffer his rest of his life in pain and agony of the crush and degloving injury he had suffered in the accident.
Therefore, learned counsel for the appellant submit that the compensation awarded to the petitioner be re- assessed.

12. Per-contra, learned counsel for respondent No.2/Insurance Company submit that the Tribunal has awarded sufficient and adequate compensation under all the heads, though the nomenclature of the heads are not happily worded.

He submit that there is no need for enhancement and therefore,
the appeal deserves to be dismissed.
NC: 2023:KHC:25292 13.

A careful perusal of the impugned judgment and the material available on records discloses that the petitioner who was aged about 70 years had suffered the degloving injury and the crush injury of the wrist, which has resulted in disability to him.
PW.2 states that there is a disability of 52% to the limb and therefore, the Tribunal has considered the functional disability of the petitioner at 26%.
The said disability when is seen in the light of the fact that he was aged 70 years and was an agriculturist, appears to be proper and correct.
14. So far as the income of the petitioner is concerned, the Tribunal should have considered the notional income in the light of the wages under the Minimum Wages Act.
The guidelines issued by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority for settlement of the disputes before the Lok-Adalat prescribed a notional income of Rs.9,500/- for the year 2016.

In umpteen number of decisions, it has been held that the guidelines issued by the KSLSA are in general conformity with the wages fixed under the Minimum Wages Act and therefore, the notional income of the deceased is considered at Rs.9,500/- per month.
Therefore, 'loss of future income' is calculated as Rs.9,500/- X 12 X 5 X 26% = Rs.1,48,200/-.

So far as the other heads of the compensation is concerned, it is seen that the Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.9,600/- under the head of 'loss of earning during the treatment' and Rs.54,000/- towards 'loss of bed rest'.
In fact, both these head are concerning the 'loss of income during the laid up period' only.
Therefore, there is no need for reconsidering the compensation awarded under these heads.

4 16.
Further, a sum of Rs.60,000/- is awarded towards 'Conveyance, nourishment and attendant charges' is just and proper and therefore, there is no need for enhancement.
17. It is evident that the Tribunal has not considered any compensation under the head 'loss of amenities in life'.
Since the petitioner is adequately compensated under the head of 'pain and suffering', 'loss of future earning capacity', a token amount has to be awarded to the petitioner under these head.

Hence, in a considered view of this Court, a sum of Rs.25,000/- could be adequate under the head of 'loss of amenities in life'.
18.

Thus, the petitioner is entitled for the modified compensation under different heads as below:
NC: 2023:KHC:25292 AMOUNT PARTICULARS (IN RS.) Injury pain and sufferings 1,25,000/-
 Medical Expenses 3,44,895/-
 Loss of earning during treatment 63,600/-
 Loss of future income 1,48,200/-
 Conveyance, nourishment and  60,000/-
 attendant charges

Loss of amenities in life 25,000/-
 TOTAL 7,66,695/-
 Less awarded by Tribunal 7,33,895/-
 Enhancement 32,800/-
 19.
Thus, the petitioner is entitled for enhanced compensation of Rs.32,800/- with interest and therefore, the appeal deserves to be allowed in part.

Hence, the following:
ORDER (i) The appeal is allowed in part.
(ii) The impugned judgment and award passed by the Tribunal is modified by awarding a sum of Rs.32,800/- in addition to what has been awarded by the Tribunal together with interest at 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its deposit.
- 10 - NC: 2023:KHC:25292
